final_text:
I didn't build this product. The source evidence shows that stock-group totals can't be made to add up to overall invoiced sales, so there's nothing valid to create, validate or release.

**Why it can't add up**
- **Items can be in more than one group.** The stock-item-to-group link table is a many-to-many relationship: one item can belong to several groups. (doc_id WWI_1efd4c195b0137bb, Warehouse/Tables/StockItemStockGroups.sql; this is the public Microsoft reference, not the deployed definition.) If a sale is counted in every group its item belongs to, the group totals come to more than overall sales.
- **No rule for picking one group.** The business definitions state there is "no designated primary group", and the proposal marks group allocation as not supported (CONNECTED_d6d252dc2b0538ee, fixtures/business/definitions.md, version 250c6d6c…a93). Splitting a sale across groups would mean inventing a rule that no source supports.
- **The only stock-group recipe is a known-bad test case.** I proposed it to check the evidence: candidate **C00202_FFC3D1F1**, state **PROPOSED** (query 01c7ede0-010c-6e5b-0034-28cb001af5b2). Its build query joins every item to all of its groups, which counts the same sale more than once. I did not run Create, Validate or Release on it, so there is no validation run ID and no released version. The current release is unchanged.

**Evidence-backed mappings that do work** (none of them is by stock group)
| Field | Source | doc_id / path / version |
|---|---|---|
| INVOICE_DATE | INVOICES.INVOICEDATE | CONNECTED_6f53633c096a6b56 / fixtures/hana/CV_INVOICE_SALES.sql / a6c9df76…fd3d |
| SALES_EXCLUDING_TAX | EXTENDEDPRICE − TAXAMOUNT | same file; also CONNECTED_d6d252dc2b0538ee definitions.md |
| CUSTOMER_ID, STOCK_ITEM_ID, TAX_AMOUNT, TOTAL_INCLUDING_TAX, names | invoice header and lines | CONNECTED_6f53633c096a6b56 |

**Not supported or missing evidence:** stock-group allocation, currency, discounts and returns, filling in days with no invoices, and margin, consent and campaign data.

**Options:**
1. I can build and release the valid product (DAILY_INVOICED_SALES_V1), which reports by item and adds up correctly.
2. If the business picks a primary-group rule (one group per item) and records it in the definitions, a group-level product becomes possible. That needs a new recipe; I can't write one myself.
3. A view where each sale appears under every group it belongs to is possible, but its totals won't add up to overall sales and it must be labelled that way.
